findings.title: `runner` context used in job-level env is unavailable
findings.message: The `runner` context is not available in job-level `env`, which only allows github, needs, strategy, matrix, vars, secrets and inputs. The workflow can fail validation, or VELLUM_CACHE_DIR can end up empty or just "/vellum-go-cache". Either way the cache location in CI is wrong, and prepare.sh and check.sh may fall back to unintended directories or fail.
findings.suggestion: Set the variable inside a step with `$RUNNER_TEMP` and `$GITHUB_ENV`, or use `${{ runner.temp }}` in step-level `env`, where the `runner` context is allowed.

fix.before:
env:
      VELLUM_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/vellum-go-cache
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

findings.title: Stale lock is never released after SIGTERM/SIGKILL
findings.message: The lock is a plain directory that is removed only in a finally block. A SIGTERM (CI cancellation, timeout) or SIGKILL skips the finally block, so the lock and staging directory stay behind. Every later run then fails until someone removes build/.prepare-lock by hand. The code handles KeyboardInterrupt but not SIGTERM.
findings.suggestion: Install a SIGTERM handler that raises SystemExit so the cleanup runs. Also record the PID in the lock and treat a lock whose process is dead as stale, or use fcntl.flock on a lock file so the OS releases it when the process dies.

findings.title: Staging cleanup can fail on read-only module files and mask the real error
findings.message: The module cache directories are read-only. If copytree, or anything else before the chmod loop finishes, fails, staging holds read-only directories. rmtree in the finally block then raises PermissionError. That error replaces the original failure and leaves the staging directory behind. The same applies on the success path: a cleanup error turns a successful install into a failure.
findings.suggestion: Make staging writable before removing it, for example with an onerror handler that chmods and retries, or use ignore_errors=True for best-effort cleanup. Do not let cleanup errors mask the original exception.

findings.title: CPU sampling via `ps time=` has 1-second resolution on Linux
findings.message: On Linux, `ps -o time=` reports cumulative CPU time as whole seconds (HH:MM:SS). The idle window is only `idle*0.5` seconds (1.8s by default), so the CPU delta is quantised to 0 or 1s. The reported `idle_cpu_percent_one_core` is therefore mostly 0% or 50% or more, which makes the idle CPU benchmark misleading.
findings.suggestion: Read sub-second CPU time instead. On Linux, parse utime+stime from /proc/<pid>/stat and divide by os.sysconf('SC_CLK_TCK'). Use psutil.Process(pid).cpu_times() elsewhere. Alternatively, have the native app report its own CPU usage.
